pages.title: Two levels of a pumping system
pages.text:
Two levels of a pumping system
Crossbridges contribute force to muscle.
The ventricular wall turns tissue forces into chamber pressure.
A pressure–volume loop records chamber work, not individual crossbridge motion.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 2 / 20

The PV plane

Distance along the path does not specify the duration of a phase.

pages.title: Ejection and relaxation
pages.text:
Ejection and relaxation
At high pressure, volume falls from 120 to 50 mL.
Then both valves close and pressure falls at ﬁxed volume.
The cycle returns to its starting state.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 12 / 20

pages.title: Why pressure times volume is work
pages.text:
Why pressure times volume is work
work = (force)(distance) = ( P A)∆x.
A∆x = ∆Vdisplaced.
Hence work is P ∆Vdisplaced.

pages.title: The sign of chamber work
pages.text:
The sign of chamber work
During ejection, chamber ∆V < 0.
Wdelivered ≈ −P ∆V.
Ejection contributes positively; ﬁlling contributes negatively under this convention.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 17 / 20

pages.title: Coupling force, geometry, and pressure
pages.text:
Coupling force, geometry, and pressure
A force–velocity curve alone does not determine the PV loop.
The missing relations include activation, wall geometry, material response and vascular
loading.
Measured pressure and volume must also be synchronized.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 20 / 20
